depth.text: researchers are trying **human-cell chips**, but replacing animal tests still means **changing rules and habits**

Emulate’s lung chip puts human lung and endothelial cells on opposite sides of a membrane; vacuum channels stretch and relax the tissue to mimic breathing. A liver-on-a-chip study **flagged about seven out of every eight drugs** that had safely passed animal trials but proved toxic to human livers. Wider use still depends on **validation** and changes to policy, training, and research culture.

comments.text: I love how far Java has come. I still prefer TypeScript since I do a lot of frontend work and prefer to use the same language across the stack. With the said, you can do exhaustive pattern matching in TypeScript! https://github.com/gvergnaud/ts-pattern
Java also has recursive patterns and (maybe still in preview) literal patterns: `switch (x) { case A(B(true, var c)) -> f(c); }`

Took me a while to get used to sealed and I didn't quite see the use. But AI seems to love it for Java so I gave it a go and now I get it. Its like a really good access control mechanism esp if you use DI and want to deprecated some stuff. Apart from ofcourse the pattern matching - which comes in handy for event driven messages where payload shape changes.
Scala punching the air rn
